subject: Discovery recap + proposed MPA and pilot milestones (Catalyx)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Wu <alyssa.wu@catalyx.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-04T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap + proposed MPA and pilot milestones (Catalyx)

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our 45-minute discovery so we’re aligned and can capture next steps for the Mutual Action Plan (MPA). I focused this note on validation of the pain, success metrics, stakeholders, and a recommended pilot scope so we can get a signed MPA and kickoff timeline in place.

Pain and context (what you told us)
- Latency-sensitive customer support scoring: current in-house models are struggling at scale (90ms target, but tail latency spikes to 300–400ms during peaks).
- Unpredictable inference cost: token costs and ops overhead are causing budget overruns for high-volume conversational flows.
- Audit / compliance: need audit logs and customer data isolation for regulated customers in the finance vertical.

Success criteria for pilot (agreed)
1) Latency: median < 60ms, 95th < 150ms for 512-token context in our staging load test.
2) Cost: projected per-1M token spend <= 40% of current baseline (after batching and caching).
3) Quality: parity with current model on the three core prompt suites (intent classification, entity extraction, reranking) — no more than 3% regression in F1 on the eval set.
4) Compliance: audit log visibility and VPC connectivity confirmed prior to production rollout.

Stakeholders and roles
- Alyssa Wu — Product (owner) — Catalyx
- Procurement (procurement@catalyx.ai) — contracting
- Ben Carter — Account Executive — Redwood (owner of MPA)
- Monica Patel — Solutions Engineer — Redwood (pilot technical lead)
- Laura Bennett — Legal (Redwood) — for procurement/contract questions

Proposed MPA milestones (attached workbook contains a detailed milestone tracker)
- M0: Sign MPA (scope, SLAs, pricing) — target: 2027-10-18
- M1: Staging integration & data connectivity (VPC tests) — target: 2027-10-25
- M2: Pilot run (two-week steady-state, performance and regression eval) — target: 2027-11-08
- M3: Review & decision (go/no-go to production) — target: 2027-11-15

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Please review the attached Catalyx_MPA_v1.2.xlsx and redwood-pilot-proposal.pdf. The MPA workbook lists milestone owners, acceptance criteria, and a short list of required production artifacts (audit log export, config templates).
2) Confirm the procurement contact and any required PO/contract templates (I copied the procurement alias you mentioned for visibility).
3) Can we schedule a 30-minute slot next Tuesday (10/12) to run through the MPA and answer any technical questions? Monica will join to walk through integration tasks.

Attachments: Catalyx_MPA_v1.2.xlsx (MPA workbook), redwood-pilot-proposal.pdf (pilot scope & pricing)

Thanks — I’ll stand by to update the timeline based on your procurement window.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Discovery recap + proposed MPA and pilot milestones (Catalyx)

Ben —

Appreciate the thorough recap. That matches our internal view. A few clarifications from my side and some procurement asks so we can keep the M0 date.

Procurement / contracting
- Please share a pricing breakdown in the MPA workbook: line items for hosted usage, reserved capacity options, and the delta for VPC/private deployment. Our procurement team typically needs a monthly and annualized cost table to compare to existing spend.
- Procurement will need SOC 2 Type II and a data processing addendum (DPA) to attach to the MPA. Can you route your SOC 2 evidence and a standard DPA template?

Technical / pilot scope questions
- For the latency targets, what assumptions are you making about concurrency and instance types? Monica — can you confirm the hardware profile you plan to test?
- We have a black-box eval for reranking that we can run against the pilot models. Where should we upload that data (S3 link)?

Scheduling
- 10/12 at 10am PT works for the product and engineering leads on our side. I’ve cc’d procurement so they can put together any PO/contract constraints.

I reviewed the attached MPA workbook and left inline comments in the file (I’ll send a separate email if procurement needs additional docs). For M0, procurement asked that any proposed discounts be shown as a line item rather than embedded in the hourly rate.

Thanks — look forward to the 10/12 call.

—
Alyssa Wu
Head of Product, Catalyx
